assessment: The current study presents an important discovery about Syntaxin 6 (Stx6)'s anti-chaperoning activity on PrP. The authors provide compelling evidence that the anti-chaperone activity arises as Stx6 delays PrP fibril formation and in the presence of Syntaxin 6, the amorphous aggregates of PrP are more toxic to neuronal cells. This study provides a critical molecular link between PrP aggregation and neurotoxicity.
